summary:
HELIOS (Health Evaluation and Life Intelligence for Orbital Space) is a software prototype developed to make astronaut health monitoring more efficient, accessible and personalized.

We developed an interactive platform featuring a 3D anatomical model and physiological monitoring panels. Our approach introduces CEMP (Cheap and Easy to Measure Parameters), a set of relatively accessible measurements that provide an initial overview of an astronaut's physiological condition.

By combining routine physiological measurements with individual medical history and risk factors, HELIOS aims to support more targeted medical assessments while making efficient use of limited crew time and medical resources. This personalized approach is particularly relevant for female astronauts using estrogen-containing hormonal contraceptives, which may increase thrombosis risk and justify specialized vascular monitoring even when routine measurements appear normal.

Our goal is to save valuable crew time, optimize medical resources and support better-informed healthcare decisions, contributing to safer long-duration space exploration. The current prototype demonstrates this concept using synthetic data, with advanced AI capabilities and clinical validation planned for future development.

HELIOS uses CEMP (Cheap and Easy to Measure Parameters) as a first level of physiological monitoring, including heart rate, temperature, sweat rate, glucose, lactate and β-hydroxybutyrate. The proposed system combines these measurements with individual medical history to support decisions about when specialized examinations are needed.We developed an interactive prototype using JavaScript/TypeScript, React and Three.js for the interface and 3D anatomical model, Python for data analysis, and Supabase and Vercel for supporting infrastructure. ChatGPT and Codex assisted with coding, debugging and design.The prototype currently uses synthetic data and rule-based analysis. Our next step is to develop and validate an AI model capable of learning each astronaut's physiological baseline.

Our innovation lies in combining routine measurements with personalized medical risk assessment, rather than developing new sensors. We considered medical safety, individual differences, limited onboard resources and crew time.

HELIOS could reduce routine monitoring time, optimize medical costs and support more targeted healthcare decisions during long-duration missions. These benefits and the proposed AI capabilities still require validation.
